[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] incumbent [[Tim Kaine]] won re-election to a third term, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former [[U.S. Navy]] captain [[Hung Cao]] by an 8.93% margin.{{cite news |last=Salamy |first=Elissa |date=November 5, 2024 |title=Kaine wins re-election for Virginia Senate |url=https://www.fox5dc.com/news/kaine-wins-re-election-virginia-senate |accessdate=November 5, 2024 |publisher=Fox 5 Washington D.C.}}{{cite news |last=Manchester |first=Julia |date=November 5, 2024 |title=Tim Kaine wins reelection in Virginia |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/4972050-tim-kaine-wins-reelection-virginia/ |accessdate=November 5, 2024 |work=The Hill}} Primary elections took place on June 18, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=May 13, 2023 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Although Kaine underperformed polling and won by his lowest margin since his first election in [[2012 United States Senate election in Virginia|2012]], he outperformed [[Kamala Harris]] in the [[2024 United States presidential election in Virginia|concurrent presidential election]] by 3.15 percentage points. == Background == Virginia is considered to be a moderately [[Red states and blue states|blue]] state at the federal level, with [[Joe Biden]] carrying Virginia by about 10 percentage points in the [[2020 United States presidential election in Virginia|2020 presidential election]]. Democrats control both U.S. Senate seats, a majority in its [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] congressional delegation, and the minimum majority in both houses of the [[Virginia General Assembly]]. However, Republicans flipped all three statewide constitutional offices in the [[2021 Virginia elections|2021 elections]].{{Cite web |title=Live election results: 2020 Virginia results |url=https://www.politico.com/2020-election/results/virginia/ |access-date=April 20, 2023 |website=www.politico.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Ned |date=March 3, 2021 |title=Democrats have controlled Virginia government for two years. Here's what they've done. |url=https://www.virginiamercury.com/2021/03/03/democrats-controlled-virginia-government-for-two-years-heres-what-they-did/ |access-date=April 20, 2023 |website=Virginia Mercury |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |date=November 2, 2021 |title=GOP sweeps statewide races with 2 down-ballot wins |url=https://apnews.com/article/election-day-2021-virginia-2bbad4e99c1a9bd4b5b943551b0ba303 |access-date=April 20, 2023 |website=AP NEWS |language=en}} Kaine was first elected in [[2012 United States Senate election in Virginia|2012]] by 6 points, defeating former U.S. Senator [[George Allen (American politician)|George Allen]], and won re-election in [[2018 United States Senate election in Virginia|2018]] by 16 points.{{Cite web |title=Virginia Elections Database » 2012 U.S. Senate General Election |url=https://historical.elections.virginia.gov/elections/view/44931/ |access-date=April 20, 2023 |website=Virginia Elections Database |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=Virginia {{!}} Full Senate results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2018/results/virginia |access-date=April 20, 2023 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}} Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in Virginia since [[2002 United States Senate election in Virginia|2002]]. Following the partial collapse of the [[Francis Scott Key Bridge (Baltimore)|Francis Scott Key Bridge]] after being struck by a container ship, Cao blamed [[United States Secretary of Transportation|Secretary of Transportation]] [[Pete Buttigieg]] for the accident, claiming that Buttigieg "spends more time talking about racial equity with regard to highways and about climate change than about focusing on the fundamentals of keeping our country and our infrastructure working."{{Cite web |last=Valentine |first=Jesse |date=March 29, 2024 |title=GOP Senate candidate Hung Cao blames racial equity for Baltimore bridge tragedy |url=https://americanjournalnews.com/gop-senate-candidate-hung-cao-blames-racial-equity-for-baltimore-bridge-tragedy/ |access-date=May 27, 2024 |website=American Journal News |language=en-US}} Later, Cao claimed that [[Monterey, California]] is "a very dark place now, a lot of witchcraft, and the [[Wicca|Wiccan]] community has really taken over there," adding that "we can't let that happen in Virginia."{{Cite web |last=Metzger |first=Bryan |title=GOP Senate candidate Hung Cao warns of 'witchcraft' happening in California: 'We can't let that happen in Virginia' |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/hung-cao-gop-senate-candidate-virginia-witchcraft-california-african-american-2023-7 |access-date=May 27, 2024 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}} In February 2023, Cao announced the formation of a [[Political action committee|PAC]] called Unleash America, with the PAC's goal being "to get Republicans elected" in the [[2023 Virginia House of Delegates election|House of Delegates elections]] and [[2023 Virginia Senate election|State Senate elections]] in 2023. However, in April 2024, the [[Staunton, Virginia|Staunton]]-based publication ''[[The News Leader]]'' published an article claiming that none of the $103,489 raised by the PAC was spent on state house or state senate elections, but were instead spent on Cao's Senate bid.{{Cite web|last1=Beyer|first1=Elizabeth|title=Unleash America was supposed to be about supporting Va. candidates. But the money didn't go there.|url=https://www.newsleader.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/04/15/pac-built-to-help-va-candidates-across-the-finish-line-left-many-confused-where-the-money-went/73264487007/|date=April 15, 2024|access-date=May 28, 2024|website=NewsLeader.com}} Cao would respond by denouncing the article as a "hit job" by a "podunk local newspaper" that he claimed was run by "left-wing hacks."{{Cite web|last1=Beyer|first1=Elizabeth|title=Candidate for U.S. Senate in Virginia responds to super PAC allegations, misuse of funds|url=https://www.newsleader.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/05/09/unleash-america-money-fox-newsmax-hung-cao-election-virginia-senate/73628953007/|date=May 9, 2024|access-date=May 28, 2024|website=NewsLeader.com}} In a virtual town hall hosted by the [[Fauquier County, Virginia|Fauquier County]] Republican Committee, Cao would also say that it would be "ridonkulous" and "crazy" for him to “drive six and a half hours down to [[Abingdon, Virginia|Abingdon]] or something like that and to stand there with four other dudes and to have 30 seconds to answer questions." His comments have drawn backlash and accusations of being dismissive to rural portions of the commonwealth.{{Cite web|last1=Schmidt|first1=Markus|title=GOP U.S. Senate candidate from NoVa doubles down on 'podunk' comments, says driving to Abingdon for debate is 'just ridonkulous'|url=https://cardinalnews.org/2024/05/23/gop-u-s-senate-candidate-from-nova-doubles-down-on-podunk-comments-says-driving-to-abingdon-for-debate-is-just-ridonkulous/|date=May 23, 2024|access-date=May 28, 2024|website=CardinalNews.org}} Despite these controversies, Cao was endorsed by former president [[Donald Trump]] for the Republican nomination.
